_comment: Hand-hardened profile for the engine itself (issue #4), in the OCI/Docker profile format.
Default action is KILL_PROCESS, so this is an exact allowlist: the parent survives only if the enumeration in baseline/ is complete.

Group 1: the engine's start-up set from baseline/*.txt. poll and arch_prctl are the x86_64 counterparts of ppoll and musl TLS setup; prctl is the engine's init setting PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 (RLIMIT_CORE does not stop piped cores).

Group 2: the isolation harness (#5-#7): musl's fork() for the child — the fork syscall on x86_64, clone on aarch64, which has no fork, allowed by the clone rule after group 4 — pidfd_open, ppoll on the pidfd (group 1) for the bounded wait, wait4, close of the pidfd, kill on timeout, write for output, exit_group. waitid/exit/rt_sigreturn are not issued today and are kept for a future harness change.

Group 3: runc's own pre-exec set. runc applies this filter and then still issues these before execve, so a profile without them kills runc init, not the engine. Found on runc 1.5.1 by running --noop under KILL_PROCESS and adding the audited syscall until runc reached execve, on aarch64 (27) and x86_64 (+clock_gettime: Go's vDSO clock falls back to the syscall when the clocksource is not vDSO-capable, as under emulation, so whether runc needs it is a property of the node). Every kill was comm=runc:[2:INIT], none was the engine. runc also issues close and prctl, listed in groups 2 and 1. A property of the runtime, not of the engine: the seccompiler test in crates/probe/tests applies groups 1-2 alone at execve.

Group 4: the run path (#8, #9), outside --noop and so outside baseline/: uname for the kernel release, and the /proc and /sys reads of the cell and residual snapshots (openat, fcntl from musl's open after O_CLOEXEC, read, fstat, newfstatat, getdents64, readlinkat; close and write are in group 2). open, stat and readlink are the x86_64 spellings musl uses where that syscall exists; aarch64 has only the *at forms. The probed syscalls are deliberately absent: under this profile their probes' children die of SIGSYS and the run records them killed, which is the SIGSYS path exercised end to end; the mount.fs probes die at their mkdirat helper and are recorded unmeasured (setup-killed), not as a kill of mount; the janitor's removals run in children of their own and are recorded the same way. getpid is the janitor's run id (#99).

Last two rules, as RuntimeDefault does them (#99): clone only without a CLONE_NEW* flag (mask 0x7E020000), which is musl's fork on aarch64, so the clone.flags probes are killed; clone3, whose flags sit behind a pointer, answers ENOSYS so libc falls back to clone. Duplicates with group 3 are intended: groups 1, 2 and 4 and the two clone rules are the engine's, and the seccompiler test applies those alone.
